PRIVATE REFLECTION: Deployment is a fixed-geometry, fixed-photometry night IR trap vs a free-form daylight RGB GBIF scrape. Test time is locked: night only 30 min after sundown to 30 min before sunrise, fixed-brightness IR illuminator, ISO 190 f/4.0 1/500 s, one frame every 30 s, camera bolted rock-face to rock-face 7 m apart with ~50 mm optics focused at ~3.5 m mid-plane. Hence at test time global brightness is essentially constant and R≈G≈B, apparent size/viewpoint are quasi-constant, and the daylight RGB → fixed-brightness IR monochrome modality shift is the dominant unclosed gap. No listed op closes it; in strict sense L is ideal.

Photometric / noise ops are mismatched: linear/non-linear brightness A,B,C, RGB channel swizzle I, colour noise J, black/white noise K inject variation never seen at test time and encourage reliance on daylight colour cues absent under IR. Scale D is of little value because range is fixed. Vertical flip E is physically impossible for terrestrial mammals. Horizontal flip F is physically plausible left-right transit and is a safe second-order geometric invariance, but does not address image-quality mismatch.

Core disagreement remains G Gaussian defocus vs H region-selective directional motion blur.

G camp: f≈50 mm, N=4.0, s0≈3.5 m → H≈f²/Nc≈20–31 m, near≈3.0 m, far≈4.0–4.2 m, ≈1 m acceptable focus in a 7 m channel. GBIF is essentially all sharp daylight colour. Depth-of-field defocus is guaranteed by the stated focus/aperture geometry and is essentially absent from training. A moderate isotropic 11×11 σ≈3 px Gaussian is the canonical proxy and forces invariance to loss of high-frequency edge detail that will be present for most field captures. 1/500 s =2 ms is argued to freeze in-plane translation for mostly axial transit, so motion blur H is second order. Horizontal flip is acknowledged as useful but secondary.

H camp, now majority in round 4: photometry/modality lock makes brightness/colour ops anti-helpful. The real train-test gap is capture dynamics. GBIF multimedia is curated, static, posed, sharp. The trap fires every 30 s with no trigger in a funneling pinch point; animals are sampled mid-transit. Even at 1/500 s a mammal at a few m/s moves a non-trivial fraction of a body width during exposure and gait phase puts limbs/head/torso at different phases within the same frame, producing spatially localised, directional smearing along the corridor axis while the static rock background remains sharp. A region-selective directional motion blur replicates that generation process, leaves background sharp as in the field, and forces shape/texture invariants that survive a small streak.

Objections to G: spec is contradictory “105 mm wide angle lens with a 50 mm focal length”; DOF numbers hinge on unstated CoC/sensor format. Defocus is depth-varying and radial, not a uniform whole-frame Gaussian; a global Gaussian blurs the rock faces and background texture that in deployment remain static and sharp and are usable localisation cues. Pinch geometry constrains depth and lateral position, travel is mostly axial within ~0.3-0.6 m body depth, residence time in extreme near/far zones is short relative to transit through mid-plane. Motion is guaranteed in deployment and essentially absent from GBIF, independent of CoC ambiguity, and background-preserving.

Shared points persist: A,B,C,D,E,I,J,K are not deployment-faithful; colour/IR modality shift is unclosed by any listed op, so in strict sense L is defensible/ideal. F is physically plausible but secondary.

Unresolved: exact DOF magnitude given contradictory lens spec and unknown CoC/sensor; magnitude of in-exposure translation at 1/500 s for typical mammals in a pinch point; whether residence time outside the ~3.0–4.2 m focus slab is enough to dominate over motion-induced streaks; whether a global Gaussian is an acceptable proxy despite background blurring. Horizontal flip F is physically plausible left-right transit and is a safe second-order geometric invariance, but does not address image-quality mismatch.

Core disagreement remains G Gaussian defocus vs H region-selective directional motion blur.

G camp: f≈50 mm, N=4.0, s0≈3.5 m → H≈f²/Nc≈20–31 m, near≈3.0 m, far≈4.0–4.2 m, ≈1 m acceptable focus in a 7 m channel. GBIF is essentially all sharp daylight colour. Depth-of-field defocus is guaranteed by the stated focus/aperture geometry and is essentially absent from training. A moderate isotropic 11×11 σ≈3 px Gaussian is the canonical proxy and forces invariance to loss of high-frequency edge detail that will be present for most field captures. 1/500 s =2 ms is argued to freeze in-plane translation for mostly axial transit, so motion blur H is second order. Horizontal flip is acknowledged as useful but secondary.

H camp, now majority in round 4: photometry/modality lock makes brightness/colour ops anti-helpful. The real train-test gap is capture dynamics. GBIF multimedia is curated, static, posed, sharp. The trap fires every 30 s with no trigger in a funneling pinch point; animals are sampled mid-transit. Even at 1/500 s a mammal at a few m/s moves a non-trivial fraction of a body width during exposure and gait phase puts limbs/head/torso at different phases within the same frame, producing spatially localised, directional smearing along the corridor axis while the static rock background remains sharp. A region-selective directional motion blur replicates that generation process, leaves background sharp as in the field, and forces shape/texture invariants that survive a small streak.

Objections to G: spec is contradictory “105 mm wide angle lens with a 50 mm focal length”; DOF numbers hinge on unstated CoC/sensor format. Defocus is depth-varying and radial, not a uniform whole-frame Gaussian; a global Gaussian blurs the rock faces and background texture that in deployment remain static and sharp and are usable localisation cues. Pinch geometry constrains depth and lateral position, travel is mostly axial within ~0.3-0.6 m body depth, residence time in extreme near/far zones is short relative to transit through mid-plane. Motion is guaranteed in deployment and essentially absent from GBIF, independent of CoC ambiguity, and background-preserving.

Shared points persist: A,B,C,D,E,I,J,K are not deployment-faithful; colour/IR modality shift is unclosed by any listed op, so in strict sense L is defensible/ideal. F is physically plausible but secondary.

Unresolved: exact DOF magnitude given contradictory lens spec and unknown CoC/sensor; magnitude of in-exposure translation at 1/500 s for typical mammals in a pinch point; whether residence time outside the ~3.0–4.2 m focus slab is enough to dominate over motion-induced streaks; whether a global Gaussian is an acceptable proxy despite background blurring. Majority round-4 leaning is H as best proxy among listed, with G as the main alternative.
